articles.summary: No g1, você acompanha a cobertura completa e a apuração dos resultados em tempo real
articles.body:
No g1, você acompanha a cobertura completa e a apuração dos resultados em tempo real

💼 Trabalhar nas eleições dá direito a folga?

Quem atua como mesário tem direito a dois dias de folga para cada dia trabalhado nas eleições, sem desconto no salário. O treinamento também garante dois dias de folga. Saiba tudo sobre!

Duas urnas eletrônicas precisaram ser substituídas durante a manhã deste domingo (4) na área da 227ª Zona Eleitoral, em Pouso Alegre. Uma delas apresentou problemas na tela na Escola Profissional Delfim Moreira, em Pouso Alegre. A outra foi trocada em Borda da Mata. Segundo o Cartório Eleitoral, a votação seguiu normalmente após as substituições.

A zona eleitoral atende cinco municípios e reúne 141.857 eleitores. Ao todo, são 475 urnas preparadas para 456 seções em 61 locais de votação.

Cidades do Sul de Minas registram ausências de mesários durante o domingo de votação.

Para votar nas eleições de 2026, o eleitor deve apresentar um documento oficial com foto aos mesários. O título de eleitor em papel não é obrigatório.

Também é possível votar usando apenas o aplicativo e-Título , desde que ele exiba a fotografia do eleitor. Caso a versão digital não tenha foto, será necessário apresentar outro documento oficial com foto.

Em Passos, a manhã foi de grande movimentação na E.E. Prof.ª Júlia Kubitschek, local que concentra o maior número de eleitores da cidade, com 4,5 mil pessoas.

A eleição na cidade transcorre com poucas ocorrências. Uma mulher foi detida e levada para a delegacia por boca de urna na E.E. Abraham Lincoln.

Segundo o Cartório Eleitoral de Passos, os maiores problemas foram relacionados à ausência de mesários: 16 faltaram e foram substituídos. Duas urnas precisaram ser trocadas e, após a substituição do equipamento, a votação seguiu normalmente.

Longas filas são registradas na Unifenas, em Varginha, com eleitores relatando demora para conseguir votar.

É possível levar uma cola já com a ordem de votação na urna para ajudar o eleitor ao fazer suas escolhas. No entanto, esta cola deve ser de papel. Não é permitido usar celular na cabine de votação e este deve ficar no local indicado pelos mesários enquanto o eleitor vota.

Pai e filha foram votar juntos na Faculdade Católica de Pouso Alegre (MG), no bairro Árvore Grande, por volta das 12h. O eletricista aposentado, Geraldo Soares, de 86 anos, conta que nunca deixou de votar, mesmo após não ser mais obrigatório.

"Votar é muito essencial. As nossas vidas dependem do voto".

A filha dele, Rose Soares, que é engenheira de segurança do trabalho e perita judicial, o acompanhou e reconheceu a atitude do pai.

"É uma emoção forte. Eu acho magnífico meu pai ter essa preocupação", afirmou.

Eleitores encontram enormes filas e reclamam da demora para votar na Escola Estadual Coronel Carneiro Júnior, em Itajubá.

🗳️ No 1º turno, o eleitor deverá seguir a seguinte ordem de votação: primeiro, deputado federal (4 dígitos); depois, deputado estadual (5 dígitos). Em seguida, serão escolhidos os dois senadores , com 3 dígitos para cada vaga. Na sequência, é a vez do governador (2 dígitos) e, por fim, do presidente da República (2 dígitos).

👤 Para ajudar o eleitor a consultar os candidatos de cada cargo, o g1 preparou uma ferramenta de busca que permite pesquisar por nome, partido, número e estado. Acesse aqui e confira!

📍 O g1 Sul de Minas acompanha, ao longo de todo o domingo, a movimentação nos locais de votação, as principais ocorrências e as histórias que marcam o primeiro turno das eleições na região. Veja os destaques!

A Escola Municipal Santinha Sales Gontijo, no Bairro Centenário, em Varginha, registra grande movimento de eleitores e filas na hora do almoço.

🗳️ Não vai conseguir votar? Então precisa justificar a ausência, é obrigatório. O procedimento pode ser feito sem sair de casa, basta acessar os canais oficiais da Justiça Eleitoral, como o aplicativo e-Título e o Autoatendimento Eleitoral. Clique aqui e veja como.

Ao fim da votação, o g1 Sul de Minas irá fazer a apuração das urnas em tempo real nas 162 cidades da área de cobertura. Será possível acompanhar a evolução da votação dos candidatos a presidente da República, governadores, senadores, deputados federais e deputados estaduais.

Eleição está sendo marcada por filas e sujeira. A frente da Escola Estadual Neca Quirino, em Passos, foi tomada por santinhos de candidatos.

A gestora pública Liliane das Merces Santos se assustou com o tamanho da fila em sua seção de votação no Instituto Gammon, em Lavras, e desistiu de votar. Ela pretende voltar mais tarde.

"Tá bem cheio, acho que todo mundo pensou igual a mim, deixou para votar na hora do almoço, achando que estaria vazio, mas eu volto mais tarde para exercer meu direito de cidadã", disse.

Para a eleitora de Pouso Alegre, Leila Ferreira de Oliveira, de 52 anos, votar é importante para garantir o futuro dos seus filhos e netos. Ela disse que procura saber muito bem sobre os candidatos em que vota e fugir das fake news.

"O que plantamos hoje vai ser herança dos nossos filhos, dos nossos netos. Tem que saber os princípios dos candidatos, pois muitas vezes não estaremos mais aqui e eles vão governar para os nossos filhos e netos."

articles.title: Monjas de clausura deixam convento para votar em Teresópolis | G1
articles.standfirst: Quatro monjas reforçaram que o voto é uma forma de participação na sociedade e que cada cidadão pode contribuir para a construção do país.
articles.summary: As quatro monjas reforçaram que o voto é uma forma de participação na sociedade e que cada cidadão pode contribuir para a construção do país.
articles.body:
Monjas de clausura vão às urnas em Teresópolis: “É uma forma de participar da sociedade” — Foto: Juliana Guzzo

Quatro monjas de clausura deixaram a rotina em um convento de Teresópolis , na Região Serrana do Rio, para exercer o direito ao voto neste domingo (4) de eleções. Irmã Bernadette, irmã Maria e irmã Mariana foram às urnas e compartilharam o que representou esse momento.

A Irmã Mariana Aparecida do Sagrado Coração de Jesus e São José, explica que, para elas, que vivem em clausura, sair para votar também é uma maneira de participar da sociedade. Segundo ela, o trabalho das monjas é feito por meio da oração, mas, neste dia, também incluiu a votação.

"Como cristã, como religiosa, a gente também tem que ter essa responsabilidade diante da pátria. Por isso, nós estamos aqui e vamos votar", disse a irmã Bernadete de Maria Imaculada.

Entre a oração e o exercício da cidadania, as quatro monjas reforçaram que o voto é uma forma de participação na sociedade e que cada cidadão pode contribuir para a construção do país.

"Nós temos essa responsabilidade como cidadãos. Estando no mundo, não sendo do mundo, nós temos que ajudar o evangelho a ser vivido em todos os lugares. Por isso, temos que participar de todos os âmbitos", contou a irmã Maria Catarina da Sagrada Face.

"Como nós somos monjas de clausura, é mais pela oração que a gente promove a cura, incentivar a procura da pessoa ter consciência. Votação e oração", compartilhou a Irmã Mariana Aparecida do Sagrado Coração de Jesus e São José.

articles.title: Lula não jogou a bandeira do Brasil no chão após votar em SP | G1
articles.standfirst: Posts com alegação falsa mostram enquandramento que não permite ver que, na verdade, presidente deixou item na mão de fotógrafo de campanha.
articles.summary: Legendas com alegações falsas acompanham vídeo incompleto. Mas  outros registros comprovam que a bandeira foi deixada na mão de fotógrafo de campanha.
articles.body:
É #FAKE que após votar Lula jogou a bandeira do Brasil no chão — Foto: Reprodução

Circulam nas redes sociais posts dizendo que o presidente Lula ( PT ) jogou no chão a bandeira do Brasil exibida por ele logo após votar no primeiro turno das eleições 2026, neste domingo (4) . É #FAKE .

O vídeo foi publicado neste domingo (4) nos reels do Facebook e em outras redes sociais. Ele mostra o momento em que Lula e o vice em sua chapa, Geraldo Alckmin ( PSB ), posam para foto com a bandeira do Brasil em uma seção eleitoral em São Bernardo do Campo.

O enquadramento permite ver apenas o momento em que Lula enrola da bandeira e se afasta dos fotógrafos.

Um texto que acompanha a imagem das publicações que compartilhavam a cena alega: "Mas que vagabundo!"Lula amassa e joga bandeira do Brasil no chão" .

Mas isso é mentira. Na verdade, o presidente entregou o item a um fotógrafo oficial de campanha, como comprovam outros enquadramentos da cena.

Um vídeo transmitido pela GloboNews e publicado no canal do g1 no YouTube confirma que, após enrolar a bandeira, Lula a entregou ao profissional responsável pelos registros de suas imagens oficiais (assista acima) .

A cena completa exibe Lula chegando ao local de votação, cumprimentando as mesárias e tirando fotos com aliados políticos, antes de seguir para a cabine de votação. Depois, ele cumprimentou novamente as mesárias e recebe a bandeira da mão do fotógrafo. O petista, então, posou ao lado de Alckmin e devolveu a bandeira ao fotógrafo.

O Fato ou Fake mostrou o post falso à assessoria de imprensa de Lula. A resposta afirmou que "o conteúdo é claramente falso". A diz: "O presidente Lula respeita a bandeira nacional e todos os símbolos do Brasil, principalmente o seu povo".

articles.title: Quem é Lucas Ribeiro, governador reeleito da Paraíba | G1
articles.standfirst: Com 36 anos, Lucas Ribeiro (PP) havia assumido o governo do estado após a renúncia do antecessor, João Azevêdo. Ele foi reeleito na eleição deste domingo (4).
articles.summary: Com 36 anos, Lucas Ribeiro (PP) havia assumido o governo do estado após a renúncia do antecessor, João Azevêdo. Ele foi reeleito na eleição deste domingo (4).
articles.body:
Atual governador da Paraíba, Lucas Ribeiro (PP) foi reeleito para o cargo na disputa das Eleições 2026 realizada neste domingo (4). Ele já havia assumido a função de governador após a renúncia do antecessor, João Azevêdo (PSB), em abril, e agora garante mais quatro anos de mandato.

Nas Eleições 2026, Lucas Ribeiro (PP) foi considerado maticamente eleito às 18h57, com 84,53% das urnas apuradas e um percentual de 64,41% dos votos válidos. O segundo colocado, Efraim Filho (PL), tinha 24,35% dos votos e o terceiro colocado, Cícero Lucena (MDB), estava com 10,75% dos votos no momento em que Lucas foi considerado eleito pelo TSE.

O g1 separou as principais informações sobre a carreira de Lucas Ribeiro na política e também na vida dele, com a formação de advogado.

Quem é Lucas Ribeiro, reeleito governador da Paraí — Foto: Reprodução/TV Cabo Branco

Natural da própria cidade de Campina Grande e parte de uma família tradicional na política paraibana, Lucas Ribeiro iniciou a trajetória na vida pública como vereador de Campina Grande durante os anos de 2017 e 2020, mas deixou a função para assumir um cargo na prefeitura da cidade como Secretário Municipal de Ciência, Tecnologia e Inovação.

Depois disso, entre 2020 e 2022, ele assumiu a chapa para ser o vice-prefeito de Campina Grande, com Bruno Cunha Lima.

Lucas Ribeiro é filho de Daniella Ribeiro, atual senadora pela Paraíba, e sobrinho de Aguinaldo Ribeiro, deputado federal na Câmara dos Deputados.

O governador é bacharel em Direito pela Unifacisa, em Campina Grande, em 2013, e Mestre em Desenvolvimento Regional, em 2020, pela Universidade Estadual da Paraíba (UEPB).

Em 2022, Lucas Ribeiro foi anunciado como candidato ao cargo de vice-governador do estado na chapa com o então governador e candidato à reeleição, João Azevêdo. Ambos ganharam as eleições à época com 1.221.904 votos, que correspondem a 52,51% da votação naquele ano.

No ano passado, o então vice-governador foi anunciado como pré-candidato ao governo da Paraíba para as Eleições de 2026. Ele vai concorrer ao cargo como reeleição, ou seja, o período em que ele passar como governador vai contar como um primeiro mandato.

articles.title: Yoga bears to resting owl face: 10 of the funniest animal photos of 2026
articles.summary: From a fitness-obsessed bear to a rather rude orangutan, here are 10 of the most amusing photos of the animal kingdom this year.
articles.body:
From a fitness-obsessed bear to a rather rude orangutan, here are 10 of the most amusing photos of the animal kingdom this year.

A scowling owl, bears sharing a laugh and a leisurely praying mantis are among the finalists of the 2026 Nikon Comedy Wildlife Awards.

In the photo above, a female brown bear was captured appearing to do her morning exercises around Lake Clark in Alaska, US. Her workout routine included some bicycle kicks as she appeared to get herself ready for the summer season.

Scroll down to see nine more entertaining photos of nature's top comedians.

This red squirrel was caught red-handed in Germany while biting off more than it could chew. The squirrel managed to chomp through the huge mouthful, while striking a dramatic pose.

Photographer Tapani Linnanmäki caught this white-tailed eagle touching down on watery sea ice on Finland's western coast. After photographing these birds at this location for years, Linnanmäki suspects, but can't be sure, that it's the same eye-catching individual that won the 2024 competition's people's choice award .

Sunbathing or posing? In reality, a visual trick is at play in this photo: the praying mantis' hind legs are hidden behind the leaf. The image was captured in the proposed Bosques del Araza Regional Conservation Area in Cusco, Peru, which aims to safeguard the headwaters of several important rivers in an area increasingly threatened by illegal gold mining.

This mountain scops owl touched down for a moment in front of a group of birders in Nanling National Forest Park in China. In the flurry of pictures the birders took, the owl appeared deeply unimpressed.

Photographer Kyo Chen was watching a group of spadefish in the waters of Dumaguete in the Philippines when the huge silhouette of a whale shark appeared. Instinctively pressing the shutter, he captured the spadefish's apparent look of terror.

When Kevin Lohman raised his camera to take a picture of this young great horned owl in Natural Bridges State Beach, California, he found himself snapping a squirrel in mid-flight, launching itself towards the owlet. Both animals were knocked to the grass below. The squirrel then repeated the stunt – twice more. Owl and squirrel both appeared unharmed, Lohman says.

Whether or not these three meerkats in Namibia were actually lining up for a family portrait, the smallest seems accustomed to submitting to grooming inspections.

This wild orangutan in Borneo was just finishing a meal when it was caught in the act of raising its middle finger. A critically endangered species, the orangutan's forest home is rapidly being destroyed.

Charles Janson took this photo of two teenage brown bears playfully sparring in Chinitna Bay, Alaska, a behaviour that prepares them for real fights as adult males. "There is debate about whether the facial expressions of these bears are at all equivalent to human smiles – but I like to think that they are," says Janson.

articles.title: West Bengal will be 3rd state to implement UCC, says CM Suvendu Adhikari
articles.summary: West Bengal CM Suvendu Adhikari says the state will be third to implement UCC after Uttarakhand and Gujarat, with public hearings and a drafting committee underway.
articles.body: KOLKATA: Bengal will be the third state to implement Uniform Civil Code after Uttarakhand and Gujarat, CM Suvendu Adhikari said on Saturday.President Droupadi Murmu has given her assent to Gujarat Uniform Civil Code Bill, completing the key legal processes required for the state to enact the law. In response to a media question about Gujarat being on the verge of implementing UCC, Adhikari said Bengal will be the third state to do so.Earlier, Adhikari had announced that public hearings will be held across five divisions — Presidency, Burdwan, Midnapore, Malda and Jalpaiguri — by the committee drafting the proposed UCC for Bengal.He had said that everyone’s suggestions will be taken and hoped that the work would be completed quickly. “Once I receive the report, if they say that UCC can be implemented, I will bring it in the assembly. That is my job,” the CM had said.A source said that a public notice inviting public representations will be out soon. “There will be a permanent office in Kolkata to accept hard copies of representations from people and rights bodies. It will also have a designated email ID for soft copy submissions,” the source added.The nine-member committee headed by retired Supreme Court judge Justice Ranjana Prakash Desai held its first meeting on Sept 3 in New Delhi. The next meeting of the committee is likely on Oct 12.The other committee members are former Meghalaya governor Tathagata Roy, IAS and Resident Commissioner Dushyant Nariala, retired IAS officer Shatrughna Singh, home department principal secretary Sanghamitra Ghosh, retired associate professor Dr Ratna Bhattacharya, former vice-chancellor Gopal Chandra Mishra, Calcutta High Court advocate Osman Gani Mullick and independent director of companies Nirmalya Bhattacharyya.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Kolkata | Silver Rate in Kolkata | Bank Holidays in Kolkata | Public Holidays in Kolkata | Kolkata AQI | Weather in Kolkata | Petrol Price in Kolkata | Diesel Price in Kolkata | CNG Price in Kolkata | LPG Price in KolkataStay updated with the latest Kolkata news. articles.title: More than 300 objections filed as Maidstone residents oppose plans to convert former Grange Moor Hotel into 42 studio apartments for 65 people, warning of added pressure on parking and infrastructure
articles.summary: Residents in Maidstone, Kent, have voiced strong opposition to plans to convert a former hotel and wedding venue into a 42-unit co-living development,
articles.body: Residents in Maidstone, Kent, have voiced strong opposition to plans to convert a former hotel and wedding venue into a 42-unit co-living development, saying they fear the proposal could put additional pressure on parking, local infrastructure and the character of the neighbourhood.More than 300 objections were submitted before the consultation deadline on September 22, with a planning decision expected at a later date.The former Grange Moor Hotel is proposed to be converted into 42 studio apartments, which could accommodate an estimated 65 people.Residents living on surrounding roads have described themselves as “devastated” by the plans, with some saying they would not have purchased their homes had they known about the proposed development, according to SWNS.‘This was our dream home’Kate Broom, 51, bought her house in May and said she would have reconsidered the purchase had she known about the proposal.“We are absolutely devastated. This was our dream home,” she said.Broom said her concerns were primarily about the scale of the proposed accommodation and the existing pressure on local services.“We have no problem with migrants. We have to house them somewhere. It is not who is going to be there, it is the volume,” she said.“It is already stressful parking, the roads are really busy. We haven’t been able to get a place at a GP surgery yet. This street can’t cope.”She added, “We definitely wouldn’t have bought this if we knew.”Former hotel was a long-standing community venueThe three-star Grange Moor Hotel underwent refurbishment and was rebranded as the Apartell in January last year. However, it closed permanently in December, with planning documents citing “major financial viability issues”.For many residents, the building had been a familiar part of the community for decades.Jake King, 38, who lives nearby with his partner and their two young children, said the proposed change was particularly upsetting because of the hotel's long history in the area.“Grange Moor has been there since I was a kid so it has always been around. To see it repurposed is sad,” he said.King said he was also concerned about how the development could affect families living nearby.“My ten-year-old son heard about it on the way to school and said he is worried about walking to school alone,” he said.Residents raise concerns over parking and property valuesJackie Farrington, 84, a former foster carer who has lived on the street for 45 years, said she was concerned about parking, crime and the potential impact on property values.“I am worried about parking and crime. We don’t know who is going to be in there. articles.title: Fresh probe into graft charges during Gyanesh tenure
articles.summary: Kerala orders fresh vigilance probe into KSTP graft claims and 2006 Malaysian engineer’s death during CEC Gyanesh Kumar’s tenure as PWD secretary.
articles.body: THIRUVANANTHAPURAM: The state govt has ordered a fresh vigilance inquiry into corruption allegations linked to the Kerala State Transport Project (KSTP) and the 2006 death of a Malaysian engineer associated with it, when incumbent chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar was PWD secretary.Home minister Ramesh Chennithala said the fresh inquiry would examine all related aspects. “The fact that Gyanesh Kumar is now the chief election commissioner will not prevent the investigation. The vigilance department will proceed after examining all legal aspects,” he told reporters.The move comes amid opposition protests against Kumar over the special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls across states. The Kerala-cadre IAS officer had headed various departments in the state before moving to central ministries.Ramesh ordered the probe on a complaint filed by KPCC executive committee member Malayinkeezhu Venugopal, seeking an investigation against Kumar. He said the complaint alleged that an investigation into serious corruption had been compromised due to external influence and that the allegation had prima facie substance. The matter was discussed with the chief minister and the vigilance director was asked to begin the investigation, he said. Legal advice had also been sought on the possibility of registering a case, he added.In 2006, the World Bank-funded KSTP undertook a Rs 215-crore project to reconstruct the Angamaly-Thiruvananthapuram MC Road. PATI-BEL, a joint venture between a Malaysian firm and Bhageeratha Engineering, was the contractor. Its Malaysian project manager, Lee See Ben, had allegedly raised several complaints about the work before returning to Malaysia, where he died by suicide.He reportedly left behind two suicide notes, in which he allegedly blamed the PWD and its officials for deliberately withholding bills after he refused to pay bribes. Kumar was subsequently removed from his post. A vigilance inquiry was also conducted, but allegations later surfaced that the probe had been abandoned midway and the investigation derailed.Ramesh said Kumar’s name did figure in the suicide notes, one addressed to the engineer’s wife and the other to the company director. On the earlier vigilance inquiry, he said: “This is a case that was hushed up. After the Achuthanandan govt came to power back then, this case did not move forward.”Responding to questions about the allegations, he said they included demands for money to clear bills and delays in payments allegedly linked to corruption. “I haven’t seen the suicide note myself; this is information reported through the media,” he said.Stay updated with the latest Thiruvananthapuram news. articles.body: Ludhiana: The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission has penalised a retail chain store, ordering it to refund ₹75 for an expired mosquito cream gel and pay ₹10,000 in composite compensation and litigation costs to a consumer.The commission directed the retail store to discontinue unfair trade practices immediately and restrained it from selling, displaying, or exhibiting expired products for sale.The order follows a complaint filed by Satnam Singh (33) of Manakwal village, who purchased a 25-gram mosquito cream gel alongside other items totaling ₹169 via UPI from the store on July 30, 2025. He subsequently moved the commission, praying for a full refund with 12% interest, ₹2,00,000 in compensation, and ₹3,500 in litigation expenses.In its written statement, the retail chain argued that retail bills do not carry batch numbers or unique identifiers, claiming the complainant failed to prove the photographed expired item corresponded specifically to that transaction.Rejecting the store’s defence, the commission observed that the retailer could have conveniently disclosed product batch numbers, manufacturing dates, and item descriptions on the invoice, ruling that “the best evidence which was in their power and possession has been withheld for the reasons best known to them.”The commission held that the store was fully conscious that offering an expired item contravenes safety standards and poses human health risks, ordering a full refund of ₹75 within 30 days. articles.title: France to shutter up to 500 schools as more student protests called
articles.summary: Education minister cites safety concerns for closures as organisers call for resumption of protests.
articles.body:
France plans to fully or partially close up to 500 schools on Monday amid a series of student protests that have become increasingly violent .

Education Minister Edouard Geffray announced the precautionary measures on Sunday as part of a bid for a “partial, progressive return to lessons”. However, after a weekend lull, student protestors announced they plan to resume demonstrations – launched last month over complaints regarding class sizes, lack of teachers, and other complaints – early in the week.

Lessons will be “totally or partly suspended” in some “400-500” high schools as the security conditions “have not been fulfilled”, the minister said. He added that 24 schools had been “burned or ransacked” since the start of the protests.

Geffray said the closures were a security precaution. Protest organisers have called for a return to large-scale demonstrations on Tuesday, citing a lack of “concrete measures” from President Emmanuel Macron’s government.

At least 170 students and 78 educational personnel have been injured since the student demos first erupted in the Paris region in mid-September, according to Geffray.

The Ministry of National Education reported that at least 400 of the 3,700 high schools in France were closed on Friday , while 560 faced protests or disruptions.

The number of schools affected on Monday would be comparable to the figure from Friday, Geffray said.

Teachers and students first mobilised at a high school in a Paris suburb on 17 September over a lack of teaching staff, excessive school-day hours and other grievances . The protests have since spread nationwide, resulting in class strikes, blockades and demonstrations.

According to the interior minister, more than 5,000 people have been arrested in the last week; 85 percent of them minors.

Critics have criticised “disproportionate” police violence in response to the demonstrations. Rights group Amnesty International said the student protestors “must be listened to, not repressed”.

In an interview on French public radio, Geffray claimed far-left activists “infiltrated the high school student movement, hijacked it from the students themselves and engaged in extreme violence.”

articles.title: SIR strikes at heart of Constitution: Supreme Court judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Launching a scathing attack on special intensive revision (SIR) that has resulted in large-scale deletion of names from voter lists across
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Launching a scathing attack on special intensive revision (SIR) that has resulted in large-scale deletion of names from voter lists across states, Supreme Court judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan on Sunday said any process disenfranchising millions of Indian citizens was intrinsically arbitrary as it struck at the heart of the Constitution.Discounting the reasons given by govt and EC to justify SIR, which was upheld in the case of the revision of rolls in West Bengal by SC with modifications, Justice Bhuyan said, "No amount of whataboutery can justify it. It strikes at the very heart of Constitution. I would go to the extent of saying that it is a negation of the constitutional order which we have adopted under the Constitution."He was speaking at the moot court valedictory function at Nalsar, Hyderabad.Nalsar students, who had opposed CJI Surya Kant's participation in the convocation ceremony recently, came in for praise from Justice Bhuyan."One last word about the brilliant students of Nalsar. You have shown to the country and to the world what a university student, that too a student of law, should be. You are brilliant, you are bold, and you are brave," he said.Detaching right to vote from citizen is like taking soul out of body: BhuyanJustice Bhuyan said a citizen’s right to vote was central to the holding of free and fair elections. “Except in the case of a dead voter, the name of a voter once enlisted in the electoral roll cannot be deleted without notice and hearing,” he added.The SC judge said the right to vote or be included in the voters’ list could not be detached from the persona of an Indian citizen.“If it is done, it will be like taking out the soul from the body,” he added. Justice Bhuyan said the Indian Constitution does not provide for two classes of citizens: citizens with voting rights and citizens without voting rights. “Any process which leads to wholesale disenfranchisement of Indian citizens, making them citizens without voting rights, would be violative of Articles 326 and 14 of Constitution of India,” he said.“If any process results in disenfranchising millions and millions of Indian citizens, making them second class citizens in their own country in the sense of being citizens without voting rights, such a process is intrinsically arbitrary,” he added, his remarks coinciding with attacks on EC and govt over SIR by the opposition and others. Justice Bhuyan said the right to vote was intertwined with India’s years of struggle against foreign rule. “It is a manifestation of our freedom achieved after so much struggle and sacrifice. Article 326 (universal adult franchise) cannot be tinkered with at all. No authority can do it, no court can condone it. No one is above Constitution,” he said.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Court throws out killer’s sentence after judge said he ‘loved’ AI video of slain man
articles.summary: The Arizona Court of Appeals determined that the judge’s consideration of the AI video was “fundamentally unfair.”
articles.body: The family of a road rage victim in Arizona used his likeness to create a posthumous AI video played at his killer’s sentencing last year. Now, an appeals court has vacated the sentence, calling the decision to allow the video a “fundamental error.” Last May, Maricopa County Superior Court Judge Todd Lang gave Gabriel Paul Horcasitas the maximum sentence for the fatal shooting of Christopher Pelkey, 37, on Nov. 13, 2021. Horcasitas, 54, was convicted of manslaughter and endangerment. The 10½-year sentence was handed down after an AI-generated video was played in court in which a replica of Pelkey voiced “forgiveness” for Horcasitas. On Wednesday, the Arizona Court of Appeals in Phoenix ordered a resentencing, writing that the video “clearly impacted the sentencing judge, who said he ‘loved’ the video and felt it ‘was genuine.’” “On this record, the judge’s consideration of the AI video so prejudiced Horcasitas as to render the sentencing procedure fundamentally unfair,” the appellate judges stated. “Accordingly, we vacate the sentence for manslaughter and remand for resentencing.” Horcasitas’ lawyer, Kristen Reller, declined to comment on an active case. A lawyer for Pelkey’s family didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment. At the 2025 sentencing, the AI version of Pelkey, created by his sister Stacey Wales, appeared to ask the judge for leniency. “To Gabriel Horcasitas, the man who shot me: It is a shame we encountered each other that day in those circumstances,” the artificial version of Pelkey said. “In another life, we probably could have been friends. I believe in forgiveness.” Lang appeared to be moved by the presentation. “I loved that AI. Thank you for that, and as angry as you are and justifiably angry as the family is, I heard the forgiveness and I know Mr. Horcasitas appreciated it, but so did I,” Lang said at the hearing. He added that he felt the video was “genuine, that his obvious forgiveness of Mr. Horcasitas reflects the character I heard about [Pelkey] today.” “But it also says something about the family because you told me how angry you were and you demanded the maximum sentence, and even though that’s what you wanted you allowed [Pelkey] to speak from his heart as you saw it,” Lang said. “I didn’t hear him asking for the maximum sentence.” The defense had requested the lowest possible sentence, but Lang imposed the maximum, saying that despite Horcasitas’ “remorse” and otherwise “lawful life,” the loss described by Pelkey’s family “could not be more profound.” According to the appeals court, Horcasitas argued he was denied due process because the sentencing court heard and relied on the AI video. The state countered that the video reflected what Pelkey’s sister believed he “would have said” and that it was “consistent” with Pelkey’s written account of his beliefs and values. But the appeals court found the video “crossed that line” from permissible to unduly prejudicial, noting that it “does not reflect actual events.” “Indeed, rather than documenting an event or recording a particular moment,” it stated, “the AI video presents a depiction of the victim and his thoughts created from the imaginings of the victim’s sister.”

articles.title: Frida Kahlo spent most of her life in this blue Mexico City house; more than 200 objects reveal how the home shaped her art
articles.summary: The Casa Azul (Blue House) was Frida Kahlo's private universe, according to the Museo Frida Kahlo.
articles.body: The Casa Azul (Blue House) was Frida Kahlo's private universe, according to the Museo Frida Kahlo. She spent most of her life there, first with her family and, years later, at Diego Rivera's side. Since its inauguration in July 1958, the Casa Azul has displayed personal objects and paintings by both artists, folk art, Pre-Columbian sculpture, photographs, documents, books and furnishings. The exhibition "Un lugar lleno de lugares: la Casa Azul", open since 28 July 2023, includes more than 200 works and personal objects of Frida's, exploring the unique meaning the home held in her life and artistic creation.How did Frida Kahlo’s Mexico City house shape her artAccording to the Museo Frida Kahlo, spaces in the house. In the "Artist's Bedroom" stands her four-poster bed, fitted with the mirror her mother had installed after the accident. The museum states that Frida lay immobile there for nine months and began to paint. In the "Studio" is the easel that Nelson Rockefeller gave her.The museum adds that her crutches, corsets and medicines attest to the surgeries and physical ailments she suffered. Ex-votos, toys, clothing and jewellery speak of Frida as a collector and lover of beauty, while the "Kitchen", typical of traditional Mexican homes, reflects everyday life in the house. With the support of ADABI (Apoyo al Desarrollo de Archivos y Bibliotecas de México), the museum was able to organise, classify and digitise the documents, photographs, magazines, publications, books and drawings found in these spaces.What does the Casa Azul exhibition reveal about Frida Kahlo’s lifeThe museum's new exhibition, "Un lugar lleno de lugares: la Casa Azul", explores Frida's artistic and personal legacy in her emblematic home. It has been open since 28 July 2023 and includes more than 200 works and personal objects of Frida's. According to the museum, it unpicks the unique meaning the Casa Azul held in her life and artistic creation, and it celebrates the museum's 65 years.The permanent Casa Azul exhibition, installed in the late 1960s, preserves the ambience and treasured objects that surrounded Frida and Diego. The museum lists paintings such as Viva la Vida (Long Live Life) and Frida's first self-portrait, along with the collection of ex-votos. It also lists photographs and paintings from the sixteenth to nineteenth centuries that the artists inherited, folk art, toys, personal items, furniture, work tools and attire. It also includes an urn holding the artist's ashes, which rests on a dresser that serves as an altar.What was discovered inside Frida Kahlo’s Casa Azul in 2004In 2004, according to the museum, thousands of documents, photographs, magazines and books were discovered in the bathrooms and wardrobes of the Casa Azul. Dozens of paintings, personal objects, garments, corsets, medicine and toys were also found. The museum calls these finds the biggest in its history and says they revealed previously unknown aspects of Frida and Diego. They were shown in the exhibition "Treasures of the Casa Azul" in July 2007. Frida's wardrobe, found in her bathroom in 2004, was the subject of "Appearances Can Be Deceiving: Frida Kahlo's Wardrobe", which the museum describes as the first display of the artist's wardrobe. It features skirts, blouses, rebozos, headgear and shoes. The museum states that through her attire she revisited her family tradition, hid her disability and constructed her iconic image.Other exhibitions drew on the house's holdings. "Frida Kahlo, Her Photos" (November 2009), curated by Pablo Ortiz Monasterio, highlighted more than 200 of the 6,500 photographs in the Casa Azul archives, grouped into six thematic categories. "With My Heart's Truths" (April 2011), curated by Graciela Romandía de Cantú, showed 138 of the almost 500 ex-votos that Frida and Diego amassed, a collection the museum regards as one of the most comprehensive in Mexico. The bright colours and popular flavour of these works served as models and inspiration for some of Frida's own.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Welsh men dying too young sparks call for a men's health strategy
articles.summary: Dad discovers he has cancer after he was accidentally kicked in the testicles.
articles.body:
Ben Lidgey was "messing around" with his son in the garden when he was accidentally kicked in the testicles - but it may well have saved his life.

When he was still in pain after a week, he sought medical help and found out he had testicular cancer.

A new report from men's charity Movember says a third of men in Wales die before their 75th birthday, and calls on the Welsh government to develop a dedicated plan for men's health.

The government said its existing suicide prevention and self harm, mental health and cancer strategies are already working to tackle some of the challenges facing men.

Lidgey, from Cardiff, says his testicle felt "like a cricket ball" after being kicked by his son, but was reluctant to see his GP, thinking the problem would go away.

"It's one of those fairly typical things that happens to men and you shrug it off and think, well, it'll get better," he said.

"I was in a busy family environment, you know, two small children, there were lots of other things going on."

After being given all-clear for cancer, Ben faced a different challenge.

He said: "I felt like I was fine but after five years my wife said 'I don't think you are fine. I think you need to talk to somebody'.

"She was picking up on the fact that I was perhaps a bit shorter, a bit more argumentative, less patient with people and just not the same person I was before."

After counselling Ben saw an improvement, and is now an advocate for more support for men and boys.

A reluctance to seek help for both physical and mental health is often cited as a reason why men, in general, die younger.

Movember's report says almost 7,000 men died before their 75th birthday in 2024. The rate of premature death in women is significantly lower at 28%.

Often, it says, men die from preventable conditions or those likely to benefit from earlier treatment such as certain cancers, heart, lung and liver diseases, those related to drugs and alcohol as well as suicide.

Where a man lives also matters, with the premature mortality rate in Blaenau Gwent about 60% higher than in Powys, while men in the most deprived communities can expect to live 7.5 years less than those in the least deprived.

The analysis also suggest the costs to the Welsh economy of the top five causes of male premature death is £1.4bn a year.

Jonathan Scourfield, professor of Social Care at Cardiff University, said: "Young men, in particular, are much more likely to get injured and die from physical risk taking. The expectation of physical strength."

He said some men may also ignore the importance of building up a social network, or rely on a female partner to take care of that.

"And then, if they're widowed or if they retire, they really struggle with loneliness," he said.

"Diet is a really important aspect... a lot of healthy foods such as fruit and vegetables, not seen as a particularly manly thing. However, some less good for you stuff like drinking heavily is seen as something that is kind of a boy growing into a man."

Scourfield said despite the decline of heavy industry and manual work, traditional images of "masculinity" persist for younger men through social media and influencers.

The report says, if implemented, a men's health care plan would complement the existing women's plan published in 2024, and would not be "starting from scratch" with many organisations already working to improve support.

One of them is MenTribe, a Bangor and Snowdonia based support group focused on building resilience and mental and physical wellbeing through outdoor challenges.

It was co-founded by Callum Tipton who left the army after 13 years, with PTSD and depression.

To combat his loneliness, the 34-year-old began taking groups hiking.

"Being active, it's obviously releasing the natural endorphins in their bodies as well so they're getting a bit of a feel-good factor from it and then obviously when they're opening up and talking about things they're lot more relaxed," he said.

Gavin Roberts from Bangor had twin boys five years ago, but they suffered twin to twin syndrome where one of the boys died.

His son, now five, has hyperplastic left heart syndrome, meaning he has half a heart and only one functioning lung.

Roberts, 44, said: "I tried to deal with it all myself, but it's hard because friends and family will rarely understand exactly what's involved."

"When I found the MenTribe group probably two years ago, I thought it'd be nice just to have a bit of company in the mountains because I was quite often in the mountains and I go on my own.

"I've lost a couple of friends to suicide and I hope that guys can just reach out and make that first step so that they can just walk and talk, or not even talk, they can just walk and be active again."

Welsh football legend John Hartson is among those supporting the call for a Welsh men's health plan, as a recovering gambling addict.

In July 2009 Hartson underwent emergency brain surgery after it emerged that he had testicular cancer that had spread to his brain and lungs.

"When I detected a little lump on my testicle... I was just ignorant of my own health - I just thought I'll get on with it," he said.

"That's a regret to have put my family through because they were living the cancer with me."

He also lost his brother to suicide earlier this year and says high rates among men need to be understood and tackled.

A Welsh government spokesperson said: "We are already addressing men's health by focusing on prevention and early intervention, encouraging men to seek help for physical and mental health issues before they reach crisis point, including earlier access to mental health support and improved cancer screening uptake."

If you have been affected by the issues raised, help is available via BBC Action Line .

articles.title: Democratic rep: Administration ‘has failed to present a strategy’ in Iran war
articles.summary: Democratic Rep. Brad Schneider (Ill.) on Sunday criticized the Trump administration’s handling of the Iran war, saying officials have not explained their strategy for the conflict. “We need to explain to the American people what the goals are in trying to prevent, and we have to prevent Iran from ever getting a nuclear weapon, but…
articles.body:
Democratic Rep. Brad Schneider (Ill.) on Sunday criticized the Trump administration’s handling of the Iran war , saying officials have not explained their strategy for the conflict.

“We need to explain to the American people what the goals are in trying to prevent, and we have to prevent Iran from ever getting a nuclear weapon, but the administration has failed to present a strategy and the actions they’ve taken have not moved us any closer to that goal,” Schneider told host Chris Stirewalt on NewsNation’s “The Hill Sunday.”

The war — which hit the seven-month mark earlier this week — has marched into October with no sign of a deal to permanently end hostilities, and 19 U.S. service members have died in the Middle East since the start of the conflict, according to the Pentagon.

Rising fuel prices stemming from Iran’s restrictions on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz have fueled the conflict’s unpopularity among the majority of Americans.

The national average price of a gallon of regular gas is roughly $4.37 as of Sunday, according to data from AAA .

Nearly 7 in 10 respondents to a recent Associated Press/NORC survey said the war has not been worth it for the U.S.

President Trump acknowledged this week the conflict could cost Republicans the November midterms but still reiterated his motive to prevent the Islamic Republic from developing a nuclear weapon.

“Well, it’s possible. It should help,” Trump told reporters Thursday. “Because Iran will not have a nuclear weapon.”

“So when you say, ‘Is it OK for Iran to have a nuclear weapon?’ I would say 100 percent of the people say no, including worldwide. So, when you say it that way, it would help. If you don’t say that, it could hurt.”

Decision Desk HQ , The Hill’s statistical partner, gives Democrats a 53 percent chance of reclaiming control of both chambers of Congress next month.

Schneider said Sunday that if Democrats win back the Senate and House, party lawmakers will force Trump administration officials to hold classified briefings with them on the war.

“The [House] Oversight Committee, the [House] Judiciary Committee, other committees will bring the people from the administration in for hearings to understand what they have been doing, how they’ve been breaking the law, how they’ve been making life harder for American people,” the Illinois Democrat added, referring to what Democrats will do if they take back the House.

articles.title: External affairs minister S Jaishankar says US has chosen to become 'lonelier power'
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Foreign minister S Jaishankar said US had deliberately chosen to become a \"lonelier power\", while reiterating Russia's longstanding support for
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Foreign minister S Jaishankar said US had deliberately chosen to become a "lonelier power", while reiterating Russia's longstanding support for India."At a time when much of the world preferred backing a military regime next to us (Pakistan), Russia was a country with which our relations were very good, and we are shaped in many ways by that legacy," he said at Munich Leaders Meeting here.He said India's Russia-Ukraine conflict approach had moved beyond just the advocacy of dialogue, suggesting India might now be looking to actively mediate.World today is marked by America’s radical repositioning and China’s rise, says JaishankarBoth Moscow and Kyiv have said recently that India had come up with ideas and proposals to bring an end to the war. Unlike China and others that have looked to mediate, India had so far supported global peace efforts — advocating dialogue between the parties — but had not come up its own proposal, reflecting its emphasis on bilateral resolution of disputes.Offering a teaser on India’s proposal, Jaishankar said India is looking to address some immediate concerns that both Russia and Ukraine have on “grain exports, energy exports, non-attack possibilities”.“We would like to see an end to this conflict. This will require dialogue and diplomacy. We have been advocating it for many years, and in recent months we have got a little bit more involved beyond advocacy. We have conversations with both Russia and Ukraine in this regard. We are trying to be helpful, starting with the Black Sea safety of shipping issue,” said the minister, speaking at the Munich Leaders Meeting here.Jaishankar had said during his visit to Ukraine last month — shortly after PM Narendra Modi’s message to Russian President Vladimir Putin to stop the “endless war” — that India was discussing ideas that could be developed for cessation of hostilities.On Friday, while Putin announced Modi had very good ideas for peace, Ukraine’s foreign minister Andrii Sybiha said India had come up with the “broadest” peace proposal out of the four that it had received from other countries, including the US.This shift in India’s position seems driven by direct domestic fallout of the conflict, whether it’s commercial shipping disruptions in Black Sea or an intense blowback from US over India’s continued purchase of Russian crude.On US, Jaishankar said the world today was marked by a radical repositioning of the US, and also the rise of China.“The current system was significantly underwritten by the United States. That underwriting is diluting.” He underlined that the sharp competition between US and China was not limited to them alone. “It has led to weaponisation of any leverage that any country has. ”Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Protesters gather as migrants brought ashore at Gosport
articles.summary: A dinghy was believed to be carrying 120 migrants, according to French media.
articles.body:
Protesters have gathered in a south coast town as more than 100 people believed to be migrants were brought ashore after crossing the Channel in a small boat.

A number of people were seen arriving at a marina in Gosport, Hampshire, having been transported aboard two RNLI boats late on Sunday. Their dinghy appeared to have set off from near Utah Beach in Normandy during the morning, according to ship tracking data.

French media reported there were about 120 migrants on board.

Hampshire Police said it deployed officers to "support our partners in the event of an emergency at sea". The force imposed conditions under the Public Order Act as well as powers prohibiting the wearing of face coverings.

A Home Office spokesperson said: "The Border Security Command works around the clock to monitor the Channel and protect our border."

They added it was "vital we continue to detain, check and process every small boat arrival".

A police cordon has been put in place on Haslar Road in Gosport, where the atmosphere at the protest mostly remained peaceful.

Ambulances and coaches were also reportedly in the area.

Some protesters stopped police vans from advancing by standing in front of them and chanting "shame on you" and "deport the lot".

There were similar scenes last month when protesters gathered in the area expecting migrants to arrive on a dinghy, but they were ultimately taken to Dover by sea .

Departures so far west along the south coast have been rare in recent years but it is the third such crossing in the space of a month.

The provisional total for Channel crossings this year is 19,451.

This is down 43% on this time last year and 23% below the figure at this stage in 2024.

articles.title: North Korea missile could put Guam in range as Kim rebuffs Trump outreach: expert
articles.summary: North Korea's intermediate-range missile test puts Guam and parts of Alaska within range, an expert says, as President Trump touts his relationship with Kim Jong Un.
articles.body: North Korea fired what it described as an intermediate-range strategic missile Oct. 3, and an expert warned that such a missile could put Guam and parts of Alaska within range, raising the stakes for the U.S. and its allies as President Donald Trump seeks to revive diplomacy with Kim Jong Un. Kim personally oversaw the drill, North Korean state media claimed, while former U.S. Forces Korea analyst Sydney Seiler told Fox News Digital that its range means the latest test has implications extending far beyond the Korean Peninsula. According to Reuters, citing North Korea's state-run Korean Central News Agency, the missile was described as part of a "hypersonic strategic weapon system" and traveled about 1,000 kilometers, or 621 miles, away in waters off the country's east coast. Guam holds strategic military importance as a U.S. territory in the western Pacific and hosts major military installations, including Andersen Air Force Base and Naval Base Guam. NORTH KOREA EXPERT WARNS US CAN 'NEVER TAKE THEIR EYE OFF' KIM JONG UN FOLLOWING MISSILE TEST DURING IRAN WAR "What is interesting about an IRBM launch — an intermediate-range ballistic missile that flies around 3,000 to 5,000 kilometers — is that it brings Guam, parts of Alaska, and Japan into range of North Korea," Seiler, a former National Intelligence Council officer focused on North Korea, said while cautioning against fully viewing the launch as a direct response to Trump. "But when you consider the preparation required for an intermediate-range ballistic missile system, it is unlikely this was primarily a response to the president's comments or actions over the past few days," Seiler said. Hours after the Oct. 3 missile launch, Trump had touted his relationship with Kim during a rally in Vandalia, Ohio. "I get along great with Kim Jong Un. Isn't it nice to get along with the leaders of massive nuclear nations?" Trump said. He also added: "When someone has 112 nuclear missiles, it is better to get along with them," pointing to North Korea's nuclear capabilities as a reason for maintaining open diplomatic communication. "North Korea simply isn't interested in talking right now, so they have no incentive not to launch," Seiler said of the recent missile test and Trump's latest remarks. "The fact that they're doing these missile launches amid a diplomatic effort by President Trump to try to re-engage the North, you have to see them only as somewhat related." RUSSIA DEPLOYS NORTH KOREAN MISSILE UNIT TO UKRAINE; MOSCOW-PYONGYANG AXIS DEEPENS: REPORT The test also followed North Korea's launch of two short-range ballistic missiles from the Wonsan area on Sept. 20, according to reports. Officials from the U.S., South Korea and Japan said Oct. 3 that North Korea's ballistic missile tests violate U.N. Security Council resolutions and threaten regional and international security. Seiler, now a nonresident senior adviser with the Korea Chair at the Center for Strategic and International Studies, said Pyongyang's posture extends beyond its relationship with the Trump administration. The latest launch comes "within the larger context of a current absolute stand down on dialogue with South Korea and repeated rejections of overtures from the United States for dialogue," Seiler said. "But North Korea has refrained from some more aggressive actions during the president’s term of office; we haven't seen an ICBM launch for almost two years now." TRUMP ORDERS MAJOR CUT TO US-SOUTH KOREA DRILLS AS NORTH KOREA RAMPS UP MISSILE TESTS Seiler warned that restraint should not, however, be mistaken for a willingness to abandon Pyongyang's nuclear and missile programs. "For North Korea, their overall diplomatic strategy is to condition the world to accept them for who they are: a non-denuclearizing, missile-launching, occasionally provoking, and rhetorically coercive state," Seiler said. "As time goes on, their goal is for us to give up any hope of denuclearization or structural change, which is consistent with them establishing a baseline: whether diplomacy unfolds or not, they will continue to develop and demonstrate missile technology." Meanwhile, Trump has continued to emphasize his relationship with Kim while signaling a wish to revive the personal diplomacy of his first term. Trump and Kim held summits in Singapore in 2018 and Hanoi in 2019 before meeting at Panmunjom in the Korean Demilitarized Zone later that year, when Trump crossed into North Korea. INSIDE THE TENSION THAT DROVE TRUMP’S SOUTH KOREA ALLIANCE FROM ‘HISTORIC NEW ERA’ TO MILITARY PULLBACK "The president has shown persistent commitment to engaging North Korea in dialogue — most recently suggesting he is open to a phone call," Seiler said. "While a call might not yield immediate progress on denuclearization, it contributes to tension reduction and helps establish a direct relationship necessary for future crisis management on the peninsula." Complicating Washington's strategy, the expert said, is Kim's alignment with Russian President Vladimir Putin. North Korea has provided troops and military equipment to support Russia's war in Ukraine, reducing Kim's incentive to engage with the U.S., according to Seiler. "Right now, Kim Jong Un, particularly given his emerging relationship with Vladimir Putin and everything he's getting out of the relationship with Russia right now, simply doesn't need to talk to the United States," Seiler said. Former NBA star Dennis Rodman's unusual relationship with Kim also perhaps offers Trump another potential connection to the North Korean leader. Rodman has also made multiple trips to North Korea and met personally with Kim. Rodman joined Trump at a Peterbilt plant in Denton, Texas, on Oct. 1 before traveling with the president toward a rally in Durant, Oklahoma. NORTH KOREA UPDATES CONSTITUTION TO REQUIRE AUTOMATIC NUCLEAR STRIKE IF KIM JONG UN IS ASSASSINATED: REPORT Asked in Texas whether he was using Rodman, who has personally met Kim, to help broker peace with Pyongyang, Trump emphasized his own relationship with the North Korean leader. "As long as I'm here, you're not gonna have any problems. Somebody else comes, you're gonna have some big problems," Trump said. Trump also highlighted Rodman's personal connection to Kim, saying: "When I wanted to get to know Kim Jong Un when we were having a problem—Kim Jong Un and I get along—but the one who knew him best was Dennis Rodman." "Dennis Rodman has a very interesting perspective in that he was able to interact with Kim Jong Un over a number of visits and get to know him personally, to develop some rapport without any diplomatic baggage," Seiler said. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "He may be offering President Trump insights into Kim Jong Un's personality, values, and potential approaches, but, you know, as I think Dennis Rodman's representatives have said, he is still a long way off from getting airplane tickets."

articles.title: 1 dead as Russian drones hit desi pharma plant in Ukraine
articles.summary: Six Russian drones struck an Indian pharma plant in Ukraine’s Sumy Sunday in what Kusum Group cofounder Sanjeev Gupta described as a “targeted attack”,
articles.body: Six Russian drones struck an Indian pharma plant in Ukraine’s Sumy Sunday in what Kusum Group cofounder Sanjeev Gupta described as a “targeted attack”, killing an engineer and injuring some others. The main structure of the facility was largely destroyed.Speaking to TOI, Gupta said the attack was not an isolated incident and claimed that pharmaceutical and food facilities in Ukraine had also come under attack over the past month. “Six drones hit the factory. So, it is a targeted attack. It’s not by chance. Actually, for the last one month, they are attacking all pharma and food items also,” Gupta said.The plant was operational when the strikes took place, Gupta said. The engineering department was hit and one engineer was killed, while other workers were evacuated.Gupta said the extent of damage could keep the plant out of operation for at least one to two years.“We are not able to evaluate the losses right now. We will come to know more tomorrow. But as per my understanding, we will not run this plant in the near future,” he added.In a statement issued later Sunday, Kusum Healthcare Pvt Ltd said total damage from the attack was projected to breach the $50 million mark. The company said its India business and management were reviewing the situation as the extent of the destruction emerged. The Sumy facility covers around 50,000 sq metres and has five blocks, Gupta said.It has been manufacturing medicines in Ukraine since 2009, including products for segments such as cardiology and gastroenterology. Gupta said Kusum is the biggest Indian pharmaceutical company operating in Ukraine, with a market share of more than 3%. The latest attack is not the first major strike on Kusum’s Ukrainian operations.The company said its warehouse was destroyed by a Russian drone on April 14, 2025, with losses from that attack exceeding UAH 1 billion.Despite the latest setback, Gupta said the group plans to continue its business in Ukraine.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Polls close in Brazil as Lula and Bolsonaro remain neck and neck
articles.summary: If no candidate gets more than 50% of the vote, the election will go to a run-off on 25 October.
articles.body:
Polls have closed in Brazil's general election, after voters queued in long lines for a tight first round of the presidential race.

After casting his ballot, 80-year-old left-wing President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva warned that the choice was between democracy and "barbarism".

His challenger, right-winger Flávio Bolsonaro, 45, said he wanted to "free the Brazilian people".

The result is forecast to be close. BBC Brazil's poll aggregator shows that the gap between Lula and Bolsonaro is only two points. If no candidate gets more than 50% of the vote, the election will go to a run-off on 25 October.

According to Brazil's Superior Electoral Court (TSE), more than 158.7 million Brazilians, including one million people abroad, are eligible to vote in the election.

Lula is challenged by 11 candidates, although BBC Brazil's poll aggregator suggests that candidates other than Lula and Bolsonaro will get only about 10% of the vote.

The TSE has not set a fixed time for the release of the official results, but they are expected within hours because voting is electronic and in previous elections results have tended to come quickly.

A victory for Bolsonaro would extend a wave of wins across Latin America by right-wing candidates aligned with US President Donald Trump, while Lula's re-election would create problems for Washington, which has clashed with his government over trade and security.

Some countries, from which Brazilians living overseas are able to vote, have already released preliminary vote count data.

In China, Lula won 56.63% of the votes, while Bolsonaro came in second with 31.33%. Lula also won in countries including South Korea, New Zealand and Saudi Arabia.

In Israel, however, Bolsonaro won 74.40% of the valid votes. He also won 71.59% of the valid votes in Japan.

Today's result will also determine the composition of the Senate from February 2027 onwards, as 54 of the Senate's 81 seats are being contested, representing two-thirds of the chamber.

Currently, the largest bloc in the Senate is Bolsonaro's Liberal Party (PL), followed by the Social Democratic Party (PSD), which has served in a coalition government under Lula.

In the last election four years ago, Lula narrowly defeated Flávio Bolsonaro's father, Jair. But the tumultuous aftermath of the election, which saw Jair Bolsonaro convicted of plotting a coup after thousands of his supporters stormed the Brazilian Congress, has had a lasting impact on the nation's political life and this election.

Jair Bolsonaro is serving a 27-year sentence for plotting a coup and is barred from standing for office.

Because of recurrent health problems, he is currently under house arrest rather than in a cell, but he has been prohibited from posting on social media or making public statements.

Despite these restrictions, there is little doubt that Flávio Bolsonaro has his father's backing.

articles.title: ​For 10 years, farmers across 13,500 hectares of southern England coordinated habitat work; one cluster recorded a 346% rise in corn buntings and a 183% rise in butterfly abundance over the decade
articles.summary: Since 1967, corn buntings have declined by 83% in the UK.
articles.body: Since 1967, corn buntings have declined by 83% in the UK. But over the decade, the bird population around Martin Down, on the Hampshire-Dorset border, has risen by 346%.The red-listed bird is not the only one to benefit. Grey partridges in the same cluster are up 147%. Butterfly abundance has climbed 183%. Turtle doves, barn owls, swifts, harvest mice and brown hares have all benefited. And it has happened on working farmland, run by the farmers and estates that make up the Martin Down Farmer Cluster, at a time when the wider countryside keeps losing species. How? Well, farmers came together, created flower margins and water scrapes, and the neighbouring farms work together to connect these habitats across their land.Two self-funded Farmer Clusters in Hampshire, Dorset and Wiltshire have recorded substantial increases in several farmland species over 10 years of monitoring. These findings are based on reports on the Martin Down and Allenford Farmer Clusters, supported by the Game & Wildlife Conservation Trust (GWCT). These two groups together manage more than 13,500 hectares, which is about 1.3 times the size of Paris.Farmers working togetherMost farmers here want to help wildlife. Instead of trying separately, they formed a group called the Farmer Cluster. This group brought neighbouring farmers together to coordinate conservation work across their land.Two Farmer Clusters in southern England were studied for 10 years: the Allenford Farmer Cluster and the Martin Down Farmer Cluster.The Game & Wildlife Conservation Trust (GWCT) developed the Farmer Cluster model in 2012. They realised that wildlife does not recognise farm boundaries. So, if one farmer creates a strip of flowers for butterflies and insects, it becomes far more useful when neighbouring farmers create similar habitats that connect with it.The farmers have an experienced facilitator who helped them identify opportunities, coordinate projects and monitor the results. For both of these clusters, that facilitator is Megan Lock, a GWCT senior farm environment adviser. She does much of the monitoring herself, helped by a small team of local volunteers.Birds and butterflies are returningThe Allenford Farmer Cluster spans Hampshire and Wiltshire. In 2016, there were seven breeding pairs of grey partridges. By spring 2025, that number had risen to 26, a 271% increase. The report also found that butterfly diversity across the cluster went up by 48%. Bumblebee species have increased by 25% over the decade, and surveyors recorded two nationally scarce ones.Martin Down's butterflies are doing well on another measure too. Species diversity there has risen by 28%, on top of the jump in abundance.The habitat work at Martin Down is easy to count. The cluster now has more than 100 hectares of new grass and flower margins and 50% more wild pollinator habitat. The number of water scrapes for turtle doves has also doubled. The farmers also look after 600 hectares of land to help grey partridges survive and breed, and the gamekeepers handle predation.All these measures have cost the farmers a considerable amount of their own money. Many of the measures also draw on agri-environment schemes, which GWCT points to as proof of how much those payments matter.“It is so encouraging to read the report on our conservation work and see how some species have flourished over the last few years. The cluster group is in great health, the enthusiasm displayed by everyone is contagious and we are looking forward to new ideas and projects that will continue to enhance the biodiversity throughout the area,” Chair of Allenford Cluster and farmer Will Dickson said.“The role of the facilitator is essential. We are lucky to have Megan, who is hugely committed and has built a trusted relationship with all the farmers over the past 10 years. That continuity is invaluable. She can see the opportunities but, crucially, rather than a top-down approach, she is out there delivering coordinated conservation on the ground and measuring the impact. It shows that if you get a determined bunch of farmers focussed on helping a particular range of species with the right facilitator, you can achieve incredible results,” Cathy Shepherd, chair of Martin Down Cluster, said.Lock's own argument is about land. “I’m so proud of the efforts of two groups of farms and estates who, by working together, have proved that the Farmer Cluster model, combining sustainable agriculture with species recovery, is the solution to tackling the biodiversity crisis. Biodiversity recovery on a national scale will only be achieved with the right support for the farmers who together manage 72% of the UK; nature reserves only cover 8%, so will not be enough on their own. The data gathering through annual surveying and monitoring to produce these reports is essential. There is currently no financial support for monitoring, which I believe should be funded through new schemes. Without it, we can’t see if the measures put in place are worth the effort and investment and, more broadly, the Government won’t know if it’s on track to hit its legally binding targets for nature recovery,” Megan Lock, GWCT Senior Farm Environment Adviser and Facilitator for both Farmer Clusters, said.Nick von Westenholz, the GWCT CEO, said the farmers deserve huge credit for these efforts. “The farmers and Megan deserve huge credit for what is a truly remarkable achievement in the context of continuing species decline across our countryside. Farmer Clusters will continue to be the mechanism to deliver biodiversity and emissions targets, and this will not be possible without facilitators, who should be adequately funded. In many parts of the country, farmers cannot afford to put extra money in and don’t benefit from charitable support. What Megan has achieved proves that continued public funding for the facilitation of both new and established groups like Allenford and Martin Down is critical and represents real value for money.”You use AI every day. The situation becomes more heated before the Indian man walks toward JohnWhatsGoingOn and slaps him.Why did JohnWhatsGoingOn get slapped during the Vietnam livestream?JohnWhatsGoingOn was livestreaming from a 7-Eleven in Vietnam when he began recording an Indian man inside the store.The video shows the streamer pointing his camera at the man and continuing to record him. The man clearly tells JohnWhatsGoingOn not to film him without his consent.Despite the man's objection, the streamer does not stop recording. Instead, he continues talking to him while keeping the camera on the man.JohnWhatsGoingOn also appears to make claims about the situation that the Indian man disputes. The conversation becomes more tense as the man continues asking the streamer not to film him.The streamer keeps the interaction going, and the situation eventually turns physical and then the Indian man walks toward JohnWhatsGoingOn and slaps him while the streamer is still recording.Posts shared online on October 4 have also claimed that the streamer had been bothering the man for around 20 minutes before the slap. Some posts accused him of making racial comments during the interaction.JohnWhatsGoingOn incident raises questions about filming strangers for contentThe incident has sparked a debate about how far IRL streamers should go when making content in public places.Many viewers have criticized JohnWhatsGoingOn for continuing to film after the man clearly asked him to stop. They argue that recording someone who does not want to be on camera can quickly turn a normal public interaction into a confrontation.At the same time, some viewers have criticized the Indian man for responding with a slap. They believe the argument could have ended without physical contact.The incident has also renewed discussion about the growing popularity of IRL livestreams. Streamers can broadcast their interactions with strangers to thousands of viewers, but those strangers may not agree to become part of the content.JohnWhatsGoingOn is a Canadian streamer who was livestreaming in Vietnam when the incident took place. Online discussions have also described him as having Vietnamese and Laotian roots.There is currently no known public statement from Vietnamese authorities about the incident. The video has instead become the main focus of the online discussion.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: US removes all bombers from RAF Fairford back to home stations
articles.summary: A statement says all bombers deployed to RAF Fairford have been "re-deployed to their home stations" in the US.
articles.body:
The US has withdrawn all of its bombers from RAF Fairford, the British military base at the centre of an incident being investigated by counter terror police.

A statement from a US department official confirmed on Sunday it had removed all of its bombers from the base back to their home stations in America.

The US did not give a reason for the withdrawal, but it follows a major incident on 27 September when police were alerted to three "suspicious vehicles" near the airbase in Gloucestershire.

Five men were initially arrested on suspicion of terror offences near the base and subsequently released on police bail. A sixth man, a UK-Iranian national, was also later arrested and released on bail.

Whitehall sources have not disputed the decision from Washington was in response to the incident at RAF Fairford.

The BBC has also been told it was a military rather than a political decision - taken at an operational level - and communicated from the US military to its British counterparts.

The UK's Ministry of Defence has not commented.

Days after the incident, Prime Minister Andy Burnham said there were "strong indications" that Iran had played a part in the incident but did not provide further details. Tehran has strongly denied any involvement.

Initially, five men aged between 23 and 25 were arrested in the early hours of the morning after vehicles were reported to be travelling towards the base operated by the US Air Force (USAF). All five were UK nationals from London.

They were arrested on suspicion of explosives offences and later on suspicion of preparing a terrorist act, before being released on bail in what police called an "investigative decision" that was "grounded in experience and strategy".

The sixth man, aged 25, was arrested in London on Thursday on suspicion of preparation of terrorist acts. Counter terror police confirmed on Saturday he had also been released on bail.

RAF Fairford has been used as a forward operating location by the US Air Force (USAF) for decades.

In recent months, US bombers have taken off from the base for the Middle East, after the UK approved a US request to use it for defensive strikes on Iran.

In July, Iran said "any base used for aggression against Iranian territory constitutes a legitimate target for our forces".

Days after the incident, and before the arrest of the sixth man, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Fox News that it "clearly involve[d] the hands of a foreign actor".

Rubio did not provide further details - saying at the time he was limited on what he could say on air.

US President Donald Trump separately said he was "surprised" the five men had been released on bail.

"We know everything about them, we would not have released them," he said, adding that the UK had worked with the US "very closely" on this.
